step1_analysis.description: A 5-transistor PMOS-input differential amplifier with an active NMOS current mirror load, plus a diode-connected bias transistor. While the paper describes a class-AB error amplifier for a video line driver, this extracted netlist represents a standard class-A OTA, which is likely the input stage of the full error amplifier.

paper_reference.title: A 3.3-V CMOS Adaptive Analog Video Line Driver With Low Distortion Performance

sky130_expected.calculation: gm1 = sqrt(2 * up*Cox * W/L * Id) = sqrt(2 * 50u * 10 * 5u) = 70.7 uS. Rout = ro_p || ro_n = 1/(0.1*5u) || 1/(0.1*5u) = 1 MOhm. Av = gm1 * Rout = 70.7 V/V = 37 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the paper's reported 35 dB gain closely. The exact value depends on the channel length modulation (lambda) of the sky130 devices at the chosen operating point.

sky130_expected.calculation: UGBW = gm1 / (2 * pi * CL). With CL = 1pF, UGBW = 70.7u / (2 * pi * 1p) = 11.2 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 300 MHz in the paper likely refers to the full driver bandwidth. For this specific OTA sub-block with a 10uA tail current and 1pF load, ~11 MHz is expected.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin at unity gain frequency

sky130_expected.calculation: Non-dominant pole at N2: fp2 = gm3 / (2 * pi * C_N2) = 164uS / (2 * pi * 20fF) = 1.3 GHz. Since fp2 >> UGBW, PM is nearly 90 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard single-stage OTA behavior with a small load capacitance ensures a highly stable dominant-pole response.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the OTA

sky130_expected.reasoning: The extracted netlist is only the input error amplifier, not the full 75-ohm line driver, so its power is orders of magnitude lower than the 26.4 mW reported for the whole chip.

slew_rate.description: Maximum rate of change of the output voltage

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the tail current charging and discharging the load capacitor.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC gain, UGBW, Phase Margin, Power, and Slew Rate of the OTA. It uses a large inductor/capacitor feedback network to close the loop at DC (preventing saturation) while keeping it open for AC analysis. The `alter` command is then used to switch to a unity-gain configuration for the transient slew rate measurement.
step3_testbench.spice:
* OTA Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}/libs.tech/ngspice/sky130.lib.spice" tt

.param W_xm4n=5u L_xm4n=0.5u
.param W_xm1p=5u L_xm1p=0.5u
.param W_xm2p=5u L_xm2p=0.5u
.param W_xm6p=5u L_xm6p=0.5u
.param W_xm5p=5u L_xm5p=0.5u
.param W_xm3n=5u L_xm3n=0.5u

XM4N VOUT N2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4n} w={W_xm4n}
XM1P N2 VIN_PLUS N0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1p} w={W_xm1p}
XM2P VOUT VIN_MINUS N0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2p} w={W_xm2p}
XM6P N3 N3 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6p} w={W_xm6p}
XM5P N0 N3 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5p} w={W_xm5p}
XM3N N2 N2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3n} w={W_xm3n}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
IBIAS N3 0 10u

* Input source: DC 0.9V, AC 1V, Pulse for Slew Rate
VIN VIN_PLUS 0 DC 0.9 AC 1 PULSE(0.4 1.0 10n 1n 1n 1u 2u)

* Feedback network for DC biasing and AC open-loop
* L1 is a short at DC, open at AC. C1 is open at DC, short at AC.
L1 VOUT VIN_MINUS 1T
C1 VIN_MINUS 0 1T

* Load capacitor
CLOAD VOUT 0 1p

.control
  * 1. Operating Point for Power
  op
  let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print power

  * 2. AC Analysis for Gain, UGBW, Phase Margin
  ac dec 100 1 1G
  let gain_db = vdb(VOUT)
  let phase = 180/PI * cph(v(VOUT))
  let pm_deg = 180 + phase
  meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=10
  meas ac ugbw when gain_db=0 fall=1
  meas ac pm find pm_deg when gain_db=0 fall=1
  print dc_gain ugbw pm

  * 3. Transient Analysis for Slew Rate
  * Alter L1 and C1 to create a unity-gain configuration for transient
  alter L1 1p
  alter C1 1f
  
  tran 1n 2u
  meas tran t_rise trig v(VOUT) val=0.5 rise=1 targ v(VOUT) val=0.9 rise=1
  meas tran t_fall trig v(VOUT) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(VOUT) val=0.5 fall=1
  let sr_rise_vus = 0.4 / (t_rise * 1e6)
  let sr_fall_vus = 0.4 / (t_fall * 1e6)
  print sr_rise_vus sr_fall_vus

  quit
.endc
.end
